One housekeeping note first: the folder-access request for the local clone was refused by your machine, so I worked from the GitHub HEAD (commit eddf25c, pushed this afternoon). If there's uncommitted local work in 12_radial_bessel, I haven't seen it. The review file is in the chat sidebar (named for the folder's reviews/ directory, with model attribution) and saved to the project; I couldn't commit it to the repo without folder access.

What program 12 is. It's one of the sixteen "dimensional reduction" lifts from Heat Note 14. The idea: write the genuine theta state m_t(u) = e^{tu²}Φ(u) as the axis marginal of a radial density R_t on ℝ³, so that H_t becomes a sinc-transform of R_t, and hope that positivity or some shape property of R_t constrains the collision observable. Note 1 proves R_t > 0 for t ≤ 1/20, derives the exact (nonlocal, Volterra-corrected) evolution of R_t, and gives a counterexample showing positive radial lifts can still have double zeros. Note 2 converts the fourth-jet threshold test into "sine coordinates" (mirror coefficient 27), and proves two obstructions: the density is not a positive Gaussian mixture, and no positive radial realization exists in dimension ≥ 11.

Correctness. Everything checks. I verified every displayed identity by hand (the generator, the small-radius and large-radius positivity arguments, the counterexample, the 27, the (2k−1)!! center formula, the coefficients in (19)) and recomputed all the numbers with independent code: the center jets, the determinant −38.049, R₁₁(0) ≈ −36289 to −36401, all agree with the Decimal certificates. Both check scripts rerun PASS. Repo hygiene is fine.

Significance — this is where it falls down. Three things the folder doesn't say:

First, the 3D positivity isn't a t ≤ 1/20 phenomenon. The exact threshold is t* = inf_r (−Φ'(r))/(2rΦ(r)) = −Φ''(0)/(2Φ(0)) ≈ 37.45. The lift stays positive for Newman time up to ~37, two orders of magnitude past Λ ≤ 0.2, so it cannot possibly see the transition. (At t = 0 it's just Φ' < 0, which is classical.)

Second, the whole construction is Bochner's theorem in disguise: a positive radial density on ℝ^d with marginal m_t exists iff H_t(|z|) is positive-definite on ℝ^d. Positive-definite functions vanish to even order wherever they like, which is exactly why Note 1's (sin x/x)² counterexample exists and why no dimension's positivity can bear on double zeros.

Third, both "obstructions" in Note 2 are one-liners from Hardy's theorem. A positive Gaussian mixture has a strictly positive Fourier transform, but H₀ = ξ/8 has real zeros — done. And Schoenberg's theorem says PD-in-every-dimension ⟺ Gaussian mixture, so the unlimited-dimension exclusion is the same sentence. The dimension-11 cutoff is a new number, but nothing uses it. (Exploratorily, dimensions 5, 7, 9 are positive, so the README's "classify 5, 7, 9" task would just return "positive"; the maximal positive dimension is 9.)

The proposed next task — control the signed sine moments S₂, S₃, S₄ — is the original fourth-jet problem with 9 replaced by 27. Note 2 admits this itself ("an exact representation of the signed problem, rather than a new coercivity theorem"). The internal same-model reviews restate the notes and never ask whether the obstructions are trivial.

Verdict: not promising; I'd close it. By the repo's own closure criterion, its findings are absorbed by the generic positive-kernel obstruction already in the heat manuscript. The review file includes a suggested content list for the closure note.

On the overall folder. Seventeen sub-projects were spun up in about two days, and the pattern across them is "exact representation + mechanism obstruction + the signed input remains open." Heat Note 14 is honest that a lift is only a representation unless the lifted system carries structure the generic controls destroy; program 12 is a clean example of a lift that carries none. The projects producing checkable new content about the genuine object are 09 and 13 (the rectangle certificates, paid dual kernels). I'd concentrate there and on the one input every project names rather than widening the portfolio further. I only skimmed the other sixteen folders at the README level, so that's an impression, not a review.

Headline. Five parallel reviewers hand-checked roughly 150 displayed equations across the thirteen folders (01–08, 10, 11, 12, 14–16), reran every checker, and wrote independent replays of each central number. No mathematical errors anywhere; everything reproduces to 25–30 digits. But every folder follows the same arc: a "lift" that is a classical identity in new notation, an "obstruction" that was either automatic from one real zero of ξ or already printed in Heat Note 14 as the stopping criterion, and a "next task" that is the Note 13 sign target or 09's orbit problem in new coordinates. Nothing in any folder depends on t ≤ 1/20 or sees Λ ≤ 0.2. I recommend closing all thirteen — six with a short closure note (03, 06, 08, 10, 12, 16), seven with a line in the README.

Two findings that matter beyond any single folder. First, at an exact double zero the Note 12 threshold test reduces (normalizer-free) to 2H₃² − 3H₂H₄ − 9H₂²/x² = 72·W(x)²·Σ_{ρ≠±x}(x−ρ)⁻² — I verified this symbolically. It's Laguerre's inequality for the deflated function, strictly positive whenever any other zero exists, saturated only by the bare quartic. So proving L(f) < −Δ at a candidate is the collision exclusion, not a reduction of it; chasing it in Hermite, score, Green, sine, pencil, or moment coordinates changes nothing. Second, folders 01, 06, and 12 each independently build a positive, even, super-exponentially decaying kernel whose flow has an all-real double zero at a chosen time T — and by Pólya (1926) plus de Bruijn, its Newman constant is exactly T. That one kernel satisfies every property any folder used (positivity, moment signs, radial positivity, Green/endpoint data, memory positivity, Ward identities) and closes all of them at once. It belongs in the manuscript as the standing control.

Specific things you should know. 01 and 02 are the same Hilbert space (Segal–Bargmann at width 2t) and neither notices. 06's "affine theta Ward identity" is Riemann's 1859 formula heat-conjugated, and its "Ward constant" is ξ(0) = 1/2. 07's slice obstruction is the textbook Re σ = 1/4 vs 1/2 fact. 03's "certified sign change" is logically equivalent to ρ_t not being Gaussian. 15's target realization is RH by Newman's theorem, which the folder itself says. 11 didn't carry out its assigned first task. And a hygiene flag: 08's "440 exact assertions" are 405 instances of local = -arch; assert arch + local == 0 — I read the source to confirm. The floating-point records in 10 and 11 also aren't byte-stable across Python versions, contrary to Note 15.

The honest summary is that the brainstorm did its job — thirteen mechanisms are now known not to work, with reasons written down — but the folders and Notes 15/16 read as though they found things, and the aggregate compounds that. The one input every folder names and none supplies is arithmetic, not kernel shape, which is consistent with where you already are on 09/13/17.

The review of 09, 13 and 17 is saved in papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/reviews/ next to the portfolio review (both untracked; say if you want them committed), and in the project docs. One note on sources: your local claude-investigation branch doesn't contain folder 17 at all, so I reviewed the GitHub main copy; if your ChatGPT work on 17 has moved past eddf25c, this review is of the earlier state.

The good news first. Project 13's certificates are real. A reviewer reran all four checkers (198–516 s each) and got field-for-field identical records, then wrote a separate 45-digit implementation of F_{t,N} straight from the stable manuscript's definitions — it matched the certified center values to 10⁻³⁶, found the same 13/12/12/13 zeros in the same bands with the same derivative signs, and put all 1245 grid points inside the stored enclosures with zero violations. The transfer bound to genuine H_t was audited against Polymath Theorem 1.3 and holds with 9% margin. The evaluator also reproduces ξ at t = 0 against mpmath's own Riemann–Siegel code. That toolchain is the best-verified thing in the repository.

The bad news. The certified theorem is already known. The windows sit at x ≈ 6.1·10⁹, t ≤ 0.05 — inside the box |x| ≤ 6·10¹⁰, 0 ≤ t ≤ 0.2 where Polymath 15's barrier plus Platt's verification force every zero of H_t to be real and simple (count conserved in the box, all real at t = 0, a collision would need a non-real pair just before it). I checked that argument myself. So "no joint zero, all simple" there follows from published results, and the region could never have carried information about Λ > 0. Nothing from the Husimi/current/Schur machinery enters the proofs anyway — every leaf is decided by |F| > η/2 or |F'| > Lη/2. The coherent current test is implied pointwise by the two component screens, so it can't exclude anything they don't.

Project 09 is a correct 27-page exact rewriting of the threshold quadratic K with coefficient-blind transforms (every theorem holds for arbitrary smooth weights, as the manuscript itself says in §tr). By the sum-of-squares identity, K < −payment is the exclusion itself; the generic sign is the wrong one — K > 0 at all 24,001 sampled points including every near-candidate, matching 13's pilot; and the payments exceed |K| by 31× at N = 22066, dropping below 1 only near N ≈ 10⁷ (x ≈ 10¹⁵), so the criterion is untestable where anything can be computed. The manuscript never states the size of K.

Project 17's central theorem is an "iff": because the divisor graph is connected, ker B_R is two-dimensional, and a certificate with multiplier norm Y exists on a cell exactly when ‖(F/2, F'/2L)‖ ≥ (1−R)/Y there. The multipliers carry no information and the divisor arithmetic is decorative; the "regular construction" line should stop. The chord/angular/reflection sections are kernel-generic and the control kernel with Newman constant exactly T satisfies all of them. The abstract is honest that nothing is established.

One remark worth having in mind as you continue 17: the sector κ ∈ [1, 3/2] is genuinely outside Polymath's trivial regime (n = 1 dominance needs κ ≳ 5), but in its computable part (t ≳ 1/28) all zeros are real and simple by the box argument, so any numerical probe for the "opposite sign" there will return the sum-of-squares sign. Both 09's scan and 13's pilot did exactly that.

The "complete theta score targets" contain no theta: D = 4C + E collapses to −β²A'' − 2βxA' − (x²+2β)A, a differential operator on the readout alone. The two "paid genuine-theta stationary signs" are correct and rigorous, but the high cell sits inside the Polymath/Platt box where every zero is real and simple (the sign follows unconditionally with margin ≈ 30H²), and the low rectangle [8, 12] is sixteen units from the nearest zero. Your README's line that they "add no collision coverage" is right and understated. The sharp residuals, the primes-2-and-3 obstruction, and the regular cell are all corollaries of the earlier "iff" finding, which the manuscript now effectively acknowledges. J₀, J₁ are Csordas's autocorrelation kernels; their positive definiteness is his listed open problem, and for all t ≤ 0.22 it's RH.

The divisor-pair identity in Note 8 is correct (verified to 28 digits) and is the first object in the whole program with any arithmetic content — but it's a representation with a signed B_P and a remaining Fourier phase, exactly the "exact lift alone" caveat. What I'd stop: multiplier constructions (Notes 2–3 close that themselves), calibrations below x = 6·10¹⁰, and rewriting Laguerre expressions as theta overlaps. The only thread I'd keep open is the divisor-pair representation, and only if someone has a concrete idea for a signed estimate from μ₂, μ₄, R_P that the Gaussian controls can't satisfy.

The verdict stands. Three reviewers went through Notes 9–22, the ~860 new manuscript lines, and all eight new checkers: no mathematical error in roughly 300 further equations, every checker passes and regenerates its record, every certified number reproduces independently. But nothing changes the conclusion, for three reasons.

The "weaker" criteria in Notes 16–17 (bounded-loss, Hölder-loss) are correct theorems that are logically equivalent to their own conclusion. If there's no joint zero on Ω then E = H² + H_x² > 0, so C₀ := max(0, H·H_xx)/E is continuous, hence locally bounded, and the hypothesis holds everywhere. I verified that myself; Note 17 actually states the converse in its last section and still calls the criterion a gain. The control kernel and your own Gaussian controls violate the hypothesis at the predicted rate 1/h — because they collide. And the Hölder budget at the certified height is M ≈ 4·10¹⁰, forcing δ < 2·10⁻¹¹.

Note 18 is a correct and useful limitative result: at any strict-interior first-jet candidate there's a polynomial heat solution with an exact double zero that stays inside the error tube, so nothing built from the approximant plus a disk bound can exclude a collision there. It's the F → H-side form of the earlier "iff" and it closes the door 16–17 opened. Note 12's "sign-oriented sufficient criterion", which the manuscript calls "the needed next estimate", is S1 with the Note-15 budget — on H'' = 0, BH' − 𝓡 ≡ −H''' identically. Note 15's new cell is inside the Polymath box; the replay gives H_xH_xxx/A² ≈ −35917, and −H_xxx/H_x ≈ 17.3 is just Σ(x−ρ')⁻² over the two nearest zeros of H_x.

One thing in this batch is worth keeping regardless. Note 20's explicit Riemann–Siegel correction (Polymath's A + B − C with a holomorphic surrogate for C) is a real improvement of the interface, and a reviewer validated it against the genuine H_t at moderate heights — the test the folder doesn't contain — with gains of 10³ to 10⁵ in the residual (table in §4). The stable manuscript's prop:diskerror and project 13's certificates should adopt it. It doesn't change where the certified cells sit, though, and Note 22 itself says the shrunken candidate body is exactly as undecidable from inside as before.

One sharpening on the arithmetic lane: the 33/41 step uses hypothesis (H2) only on the D^{5/41} sixth-power rows, and on those rows A_{p⁶} is A₁ with p masked, so what's consumed is |A₁| ≪ D^{33/41} — the conclusion — with the 11/12 strip paying only the masks.

The brainstorm is at papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/brainstorm/NEW_PATHS_FORWARD_BRAINSTORM_CLAUDE_20261011.md (new folder, untracked) and in the project docs. I also had a reviewer build a precise digest of the four arithmetic lanes and the character-amplification folder — every target estimate, every mechanism tried and what killed it, every imported lemma — which fed the document; I can save that digest alongside it if you want it in the repo.

The framing that drives it. Two things fall out of lining up what quasi-RH at 11/12 or 7/8 actually provides against what is already known unconditionally. In the heat lane it provides nothing: de Bruijn gives Λ ≤ δ²/2 = 0.347 or 0.281, worse than the unconditional 0.2, and the strip only beats 0.2 for σ₀ < 0.816. So everything in newman_collisions was an unconditional attack on Λ = 0, which is RH itself. And on the arithmetic side the hypothesis is weaker than Bourgain on the line and barely stronger than Guth–Maynard on density; the only thing it uniquely supplies is a power saving in prime and Möbius sums. A descent has to consume that — and a self-improving Möbius exponent is a bootstrap that does not exist in the literature for a single L-function. Known strips come from positivity across a family or from geometry, never from a local bootstrap. The digest confirmed the shape: every lane's open estimate is "beat the large sieve by a fixed power for Möbius-weighted sums over a family of length below the conductor", which for an individual member is a zero-free strip for that member. The lanes are asking the external preprints' question again, one level down.

Where I'd put effort, in order. D1: find the family-to-individual step in the two external proofs — the one place in the whole program where an individual strip is (claimed to be) produced from averages, and therefore the only candidate descent engine; the audits checked local algebra but never asked which step makes the statement hold for the trivial character. D2: turn the "hypothesis equals conclusion" finding into an automatic gate (random multiplicative model, the control kernel, coherent-row restriction). D3: a function-field testbed, where the needed moments are theorems and zeros are exact, to check whether the reduction structure is even consistent with a known RH world. D4: the one real deliverable the heat machinery can produce — pushing Λ ≤ 0.2 with the corrected Riemann–Siegel interface and the certified evaluator (the dominance ceiling at X = 6·10¹² is about 0.19). D5: write the arithmetic problem once, with known tools and their limits, and stop reducing it to itself. D6: derive one checkable consequence of the ~20 imported lemmas before building more on them.

Two mechanisms I tried myself and discarded are recorded so they don't get reinvented: "zero pressure" from the dynamics ODE (it is the physics behind first-term dominance and is numerically weaker than it at every height), and a reverse de Bruijn bound tying strip width to Λ (z³ − 3z under forward heat is a counterexample). There's also a wild-card section (Li's criterion, Weil positivity with limited support, weighted Nyman–Beurling, Rodgers–Tao in reverse) with why each doesn't descend, and a stop list.
